title: Structures — Inspection and Re-Treatment of the Lower Shell Lap Joint Land
abstract: Inspect and re-treat the lower shell lap joint land to the revised two-stage surface treatment practice, on aircraft delivered before the joining station process was corrected.

sections.planning_reason: Filiform corrosion under the paint film at the lower shell lap joint land has been reported by seven operators, all based in humid coastal environments, with the earliest finding at four years in service. Forty-one findings have been recorded across the fleet in three years and eleven went past the blend-out limit and needed an engineering disposition. The mechanism is the surface treatment having been applied outside its stated window on the joining station, and a sealing practice that leaves a capillary path at the fastener head.
sections.description: The bulletin opens the lower shell lap joint land inside the cargo compartments and the belly fairing, inspects for filiform corrosion, blends out any finding within limits and re-treats the land to the two-stage practice with the revised sealing sequence.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the lower shell in the cargo compartments, zones 131 and 141, and open the belly fairing at zone 191. Remove the floor and lining panels along the joint run. Do a detailed visual inspection of the joint land under magnification and record every finding with its length and depth. Blend out findings inside the allowable damage limits and refer any finding outside them to the repair scheme. Do the eddy current inspection at every blended area. Apply the two-stage surface treatment to the practice on drawings D51201114548 and D51201185443, keeping to the ninety minute window after abrasion. Install the shear tie D5120110715725 and the strap D5120111806797 at the new treatment standard where either has been removed. Install the edging grommet AES445369-54 at every cable pass-through crossing the treated land. Apply the sealing bead and check the drain path. Install the panels and record the embodiment and the finding list.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00001 to MSN C00544 built before the joining station process was corrected. One aircraft already re-worked under an engineering disposition is excluded. There is no pre-modification or post-modification condition.
sections.material_note: Kit K5120-2001-01 contains the treatment and sealing materials, the grommet set and the replacement shear ties and straps needed for a typical finding population. Lead time is eight weeks. Operators should expect to order additional structural items after the inspection step.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled heavy check, or within sixty months of the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first. Operators based in humid coastal environments should plan the earlier opportunity.
